checks.name: F09-R5-B shutdown precision: 100 ms grace deadline qualified and callback completion required
checks.command_or_evidence: inspection of the GatewayGrpcServer file @details and @lifetime and the destructor @brief in src/xverse/xcom/include/xverse/xcom/tool_gateway_grpc.hpp and the file @details in src/xverse/xcom/src/tool_gateway_grpc.cpp against GatewayGrpcServer::~GatewayGrpcServer in the same source
checks.measured: The cpp file block and the header @lifetime and destructor @brief now state that destruction marks the service shutting down, requests gRPC shutdown with a 100 ms grace deadline before forced cancellation, joins the poller, disconnects the session, and unlinks the socket, and that the deadline bounds only the grace period before forced cancellation: it does not preempt or bound an executing RPC callback, so destructor completion still requires those callbacks to return and must not be documented as a fixed 100 ms bound. The implementation matches exactly: the destructor stores active_=false, calls service_.request_shutdown(), server_->Shutdown(now + std::chrono::milliseconds(100)), poller_.join(), service_.disconnect(), and ::unlink. The prior unqualified 'bounded server shutdown and destructor cleanup' wording is gone, restoring consistency with the admitted callback-completion limitation and adding no callback preemption or fixed total-destruction bound.
